definition: Maximum Variance Unfolding (MVU), also known as Semidefinite Embedding (SDE), is an algorithm in computer science that uses semidefinite programming to perform non-linear dimensionality reduction of high-dimensional vectorial input data.
details: It is motivated by the observation that kernel Principal Component Analysis (kPCA) does not reduce the data dimensionality, as it leverages the Kernel trick to non-linearly map the original data into an inner-product space.

explainer.lead: Semidefinite embedding, also called Maximum Variance Unfolding, performs non-linear dimensionality reduction of high-dimensional vector data using semidefinite programming. It exists because kernel PCA does not actually reduce dimensionality.

tiers.eli5: It squashes complicated high-dimensional data into fewer dimensions while keeping the data spread out as much as possible.
tiers.practitioner: It is used when a non-linear reduction is needed and the kernel trick alone is not enough. A pitfall is that semidefinite programming is costly, so it suits modest datasets better than large ones.
tiers.paperLevel: Maximum Variance Unfolding (MVU), or Semidefinite Embedding (SDE), uses semidefinite programming for non-linear dimensionality reduction; it is motivated by kernel PCA not reducing data dimensionality since the kernel trick maps data into an inner-product space.

explainer.example: A set of high-dimensional vectors is reduced to a low-dimensional layout by solving a semidefinite program that maximises variance.
